findings.F1: The tested relation sits almost entirely at the top of the 30-day range. Closes in the top fifth of the range (position 0.78 to 1) were followed by +3.03 % over 10 days beyond the coin's mean (t 2.36, 252 non-overlapping cases). Every other fifth was below the mean, from -0.38 % (t -0.43) at the bottom to -0.96 % (t -1.04) in the middle. Coins near their 30-day low did not keep falling.
findings.F2: Closes within 1.8 % of the 30-day closing high were followed by +3.58 % over 10 days beyond the mean (t 2.44, 210 cases). The next five sixths of distance from the high ranged from -1.33 % to +0.66 %, all with |t| < 1.6. The same top sixth measured in the coin's daily-volatility units gave +3.14 % (t 2.12). For the 60-day high it gave +3.23 % (t 2.43, 138 cases).
findings.F3: Bars that closed on a new 30-day closing high were followed by +4.69 % over 10 days (t 2.28, 137 cases). The effect fades within days: one to two days after the high it was -0.84 % (t -0.81), and from 5 to 30 days after it was -1.23 % to -0.20 %. This finding is partly carried by one coin: XRP contributed +22.9 % (t 2.24, 18 cases), against BTC's +2.9 % (t 1.66) and +1.2 % to +2.9 % in the other coins.
findings.F4: The idea's slope (10-day excess return on range position) depends on the coin's own 60-day return. It was 0.0387 (t 2.88, 423 cases) when the 60-day return was positive and -0.0043 (t -0.38, 404 cases) when it was negative. By size of the 30-day move it was 0.0182 (t 1.51) in the trending third and 0.0073 (t 0.73) in the flattest third.
findings.F5: The brief's mean reversion does not show in flat coins either. In the flattest third of 30-day moves the slope is +0.0073 (t 0.73), and in the narrowest third of 30-day ranges it is -0.0015 (t -0.16). So neither the tested continuation nor the brief's reversion holds there.
findings.F6: The relation is unstable across years. The slope was positive in 2020 (t 2.67) and 2019/2021 (t 1.22/1.56), and negative in 2018 (t -2.26), 2022 (t -1.96) and 2023 (t -2.16). By coin, only XRP (t 2.08) and ETH (t 1.73) carry it, while BTC, LTC and XMR have |t| < 0.3.
findings.F7: Coins rose more on Saturdays: +0.454 % a day (t 5.53, 2484 days) against +0.01 % on the other days excluding Friday. Saturday minus the rest gives a Welch t of 4.26. This held in all six coins (t 1.40 to 2.92) and in six of eight years (2022: t 0.42, 2023: t -0.01).
findings.F8: The book is not a disguised market bet. Its daily returns correlate -0.047 with the coins'. On its worst 5 % of days (-4.28 %) the coins moved +0.04 %, and on its best 5 % (+4.53 %) the coins moved -0.34 %. Its Saturday mean of +0.167 % is its largest weekday.
findings.F9: The tested cost of a trade is 0.19 %. The move per case in the top fifth of the range (+3.03 %, F1) and at new highs (+4.69 %, F3) is 15 to 25 times that cost. The tested idea's average over all cases is only 0.33 %.

ideas.idea: The closer a coin's daily close is to its 30-day closing high, the more the coin rises over the next 10 days, with the largest rise following closes at the high itself.
ideas.consequence: A trader can buy coins closing at or just under their monthly high and should refuse to short them, rather than spread bets across the whole range.
ideas.name: near-high continuation over ten days

ideas.idea: When a coin's 60-day return is positive, the higher its daily close sits above the middle of its 30-day closing range, the more it keeps rising over the next 10 days. The larger the 60-day rise, the stronger this effect.
ideas.consequence: A trader can lean with range position only in coins that are up over two months, and should ignore range position in coins that are down.
ideas.name: range continuation in uptrending coins

ideas.idea: The higher a coin has closed above its 30-day closing high on a given day, the larger its rise over the next 10 days, with the effect fading over the days after the high.
ideas.consequence: A trader can act on a fresh monthly breakout on its own day, and should not chase a high already a few days old.
ideas.name: fresh breakout fading follow-through
